items.item: A per-file Bloom filter lets a read skip an SSTable without touching disk: hash the key, probe those bits, and a single zero bit proves the key is absent from that file.

items.item: A Bloom filter can be wrong in only one direction: it never gives a false negative, but it can give a false positive, forcing a wasted read of a file that doesn't actually hold the key.

at.step: Reveal: the Bloom filter, a fast no

items.item: After a Bloom filter passes, a per-file block index (a binary-search structure over that file's data blocks) finds the one data block that might hold the key, without scanning the whole file.

at.step: Reveal: the block index, after the filter says maybe

items.item: A range read can't stop at the first match: it must scan every live structure's overlap with the range and merge the results (newest version of each key wins), typically via a priority queue.

items.item: A delete is written as a new record, a tombstone, not an in-place removal; it occupies real space on disk until a later compaction discards it.
